description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
PRE-EXISTING.  perl-tests/scalar.t lines 400-480 ([perl #109828]).

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv): perl-tests/scalar.t 88, 89, 91, 92,
104, 106, 111, 112, 114 = 9 rows; plus 94 and 116 which are the WARNING half and
belong to #221 as well.

PERL'S RULE: PerlIO::scalar maps BYTES.  `open($fh, "<", \$content)` where
$content holds a character above 0xFF FAILS, sets $! = EINVAL (22), and under
`use warnings "utf8"` warns
    Strings with code points over 0xFF may not be mapped into in-memory file handles
A read or a print through an already-open handle whose target BECOMES
non-downgradable fails the same way.  A merely utf8-UPGRADED but downgradable
target (e.g. "12\xA1") opens and reads the downgraded bytes -- PCL gets that
half right (scalar.t rows 95-99 pass).

PCL: the open succeeds, $! stays 0, read() returns the character, print()
succeeds.  Rows read got='' / '1' / '0' against exp='' fail / EINVAL / undef.

The root is the missing per-SV utf8 flag (docs/not-supported.md 'Unicode
semantics differences'), but the OBSERVABLE here is not a flag readout: it is an
open that must fail and an errno that must be set, so it is a bug, not that
entry's ruled non-support.  A "does this string hold a code point > 0xFF"
predicate is all the decision needs.
subject: BUG (in-memory filehandle): a target with code points > 0xFF is accepted; perl refuses it with EINVAL (and warns under `use warnings "utf8"`) -- 9 blessed rows in perl-tests/scalar.t
